message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of J.K. Rowling’s most popular books:

| Title | Year Published | Notes |
|-------|----------------|-------|
| **Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone** (titled *Sorcerer’s Stone* in the U.S.) | 1997 | First book in the globally‑famous Harry Potter series; introduces Hogwarts, magic, and the main characters. |
| **Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets** | 1998 | Second installment; follows Harry’s return to school and the mystery of the hidden chamber. |
| **Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban** | 1999 | Third book; introduces Sirius Black and the Marauder’s Map. |
| **Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire** | 2000 | Fourth book; features the Triwizard Tournament and the rise of Voldemort. |
| **Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix** | 2003 | Fifth book; focuses on the formation of Dumbledore’s Army and the Ministry’s denial of Voldemort’s return. |
| **Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince** | 2005 | Sixth book; delves into Voldemort’s past and the discovery of Horcruxes. |
| **Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows** | 2007 | Final book; concludes the epic saga with the Battle of Hogwarts. |
| **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel; a political thriller set in a small English town. |
| **The Cuckoo’s Calling** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2013 | Debut crime novel under her pseudonym; follows private detective Cormoran Strike. |
| **The Silkworm** | 2014 | Second book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Career of Evil** | 2015 | Third book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Lethal White** | 2018 | Fourth book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Troubled Blood** | 2020 | Fifth book in the Cormoran Strike series. |

These titles cover both her iconic fantasy world and her ventures into adult fiction, showcasing her versatility as an author.
